ROLE: Hand out a borrowed write slot directly after the last valid byte together with the number of bytes that may be written there; storage is unchanged.

STRUCT.NAME: struct byte_buf
STRUCT.ROLE: buffer whose spare tail is exposed

LOGIC.INPUT: buf (NULL allowed) and an optional size_t out-parameter avail.
LOGIC.ACTION: If buf is NULL, write 0 through avail when avail is not NULL and return NULL. Otherwise compute spare = buf->cap - buf->len and write it through avail when avail is not NULL. Return buf->data + buf->len when buf->data is not NULL; return NULL when buf->data is NULL (no storage allocated yet), so the caller must call buffer_reserve before writing. The returned pointer borrows storage owned by buf and stays valid only until the next buffer operation that reallocates or consumes bytes.
LOGIC.OUTPUT: A borrowed pointer to the first unwritten byte plus the writable byte count through *avail; NULL when no storage is allocated.
INVARIANTS_USED: the tail is never part of the valid length until buffer_commit
pointer arithmetic is performed only on non-NULL data
LOGIC.PRECONDITION: buf is NULL or a valid buffer.
LOGIC.POSTCONDITION: *avail == cap - len and the returned pointer is data + len or NULL; data/len/cap unchanged.
LOGIC.THREAD_SAFETY: Not thread safe; the caller owns the buffer exclusively.
